title: Persistent state quality, and a two-level memory for the recall loss
follows: R1.01 / R1.01b: the fixed-size state loses on recall (P3), as predicted by its capacity
question: What does the persistent state encode (facts, intermediate results, calibrated uncertainty), and does a small active state plus a constant-size exact slot memory with top-k reads close the recall gap to a Transformer at <= 1/4 of its KV-cache bytes, without losing state tracking or hops?

compute.note: rouge-b: 166 MFLOP forward x 3 x 64 x 15,000

predictions.M1_recall: rouge-mem OOD recall >= rouge-b + 0.10 and >= transformer - 0.02, with inference memory at 26 facts <= 0.25x the Transformer's KV cache.
predictions.M2_no_regression: rouge-mem OOD state and OOD hops each >= rouge-b - 0.02.
predictions.M3_facts_probe: A linear probe reads 'is key x stored' (balanced accuracy) from rouge-mem's state + memory at least as well as from rouge-b's state (OOD lengths). Added before any run: an untrained rouge-mem already scores ~0.89 on this probe (raw slot storage is linearly decodable), so M3 also requires the trained model to beat the same architecture untrained. Every probe is reported trained / untrained. M3 does not enter the decision.
predictions.probes_reported: Probes for intermediate results (state value half way; first hop) and ECE (uncertainty) are reported for every model, not gating. Goals and causal relations are not tested here: no task in this benchmark has them.

decision.PASS: M1 and M2: the two-level memory is kept for the combined model.
decision.PARTIAL: Recall improves by >= 0.10 over rouge-b but M1 or M2 is otherwise missed.
decision.FAIL: No recall gain of 0.10 over rouge-b: the memory design is recorded and not scaled.

prior_art: Neural Turing Machines, Graves et al. 2014 (arXiv 1410.5401)
Differentiable Neural Computer, Graves et al. 2016
Repeat After Me, Jelassi et al. 2024 (arXiv 2402.01032): fixed-state models lose on copying/recall
not_claimed: Slot memories, content addressing and top-k reads are prior art. No novelty claim.
benchmark_note: Changed before any run (2026-09-29): microbench v1's hops task let 'the digit at the end of the longest chain' answer 91% ID / 100% OOD without following the query (found while auditing R1.02's benchmark). microbench2 uses two equal chains (50% guess); state and recall are unchanged. tests/test_r103.py audits cues. Models, budget and gate thresholds are unchanged.
